mainTopic: Liability of people who fall one after another on a public road, and the start of the משנה about a barrel broken on a beam.
overview: The גמרא explains רבא's ruling about people who trip one after another on a public road. The first person is a פושע and pays for everything. The second pays only for damage his body causes, not for damage his fallen property causes. A ברייתא seems to exempt everyone, even the first, for property damage, and the attempts to read 'כולן' as excluding the first do not hold up. So the גמרא tries a new reading of רבא: the fallen second person is like a בור, and a בור is exempt for כלים. That reading works for שמואל but not for רב, so the גמרא returns to the original reading. It explains the ברייתא as a case of כלים broken by כלים. Then רב פפא and רב זביד describe how everyone could fall because of the first person. A new משנה begins: when a barrel breaks on a beam, the beam carrier is פטור, whether the two walk toward each other or the beam carrier walks in front.

steps.title: Why the first is fully liable and the second only partly
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains רבא's ruling. The first person is a פושע and pays for everything. The second pays for damage caused by his body, because he should have gotten up. He is exempt for damage caused by his property, because he did not create the obstacle.
steps.simpleTranslation: The first one is definitely negligent. The second one is liable for damage his body causes, because he should have stood up and did not. He is exempt for damage his property causes, because he can say: 'I didn't dig this pit.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is giving the reasons behind רבא's ruling about a chain of people falling on the road.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first person caused the whole mess by falling, so he is a פושע and pays for both his body and his property. The second person was knocked down by someone else. He is blamed only for not getting up, which is his body's fault. The things he dropped are there because of the first person, so they are not his fault.

keyTerms.meaning: Negligent; someone who acted carelessly and is responsible
For his body; damage caused by the person himself
For his property; damage caused by his belongings
A pit; used here to mean an obstacle someone created

steps.confusionAlert: The second person is not totally exempt. He is liable for damage caused by his body and exempt only for damage caused by his property.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the split between נזקי גופו and נזקי ממונו that the ברייתא in the next step seems to contradict.

phrases.english: The first one is certainly negligent.
The second one is liable for damage caused by his body,
because he should have stood up and he did not stand up.
For damage caused by his property he is exempt,
because he can say to him:
This pit, I did not dig it.
phrases.notes: A way of saying: I'm not the one who put this obstacle here. The first person caused it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the reasoning of רבא's ruling, which was stated just before this section.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The first is a פושע and liable for body and property. The second is liable for body damage only, because he should have stood up. He is exempt for property damage because he did not create the obstacle.

steps.title: A ברייתא seems to exempt even the first for property damage
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says all of them are liable for body damage and exempt for property damage. This seems to include the first person, which contradicts רבא.
steps.simpleTranslation: They raised an objection: 'All of them are liable for damage caused by their bodies and exempt for damage caused by their property.' Doesn't that mean even the first?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבא with a ברייתא that seems to exempt everyone, the first person included, for property damage.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא said the first person pays even for damage caused by his property. The ברייתא says 'all of them' are exempt for property damage. If 'all' includes the first, the ברייתא contradicts רבא.

phrases.english: They raised an objection:
All of them are liable for damage caused by their bodies,
and exempt for damage caused by their property.
What, does this not mean even the first?

steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's ruling that the first person is liable for damage caused by his property.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא says 'all of them' are exempt for property damage. Read simply, that includes the first person, which contradicts רבא.

steps.title: The ברייתא means everyone except the first
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the ברייתא is talking about everyone except the first person.
steps.simpleTranslation: No, it means everyone except the first.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רבא by limiting the ברייתא so that it does not include the first person.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the ברייתא leaves out the first person, it only exempts the later ones for property damage. That matches רבא exactly, since he also exempts the second for property damage.

phrases.english: No, it means except for the first.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing the scope of the ברייתא
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'All of them' includes the first person.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא refers to everyone except the first, so it agrees with רבא.

steps.title: But the ברייתא says 'all of them'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא pushes back: the ברייתא clearly says 'all of them', which sounds like it includes the first.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the answer just given by pointing to the word 'all'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'כולם' sounds like it includes every person in the case. Leaving out the first person seems to go against the plain wording.

keyTerms.meaning: But it teaches; used to point to wording that seems to contradict an answer

phrases.english: But it teaches "all of them"!

steps.kashyaTarget: The answer that the ברייתא excludes the first person.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The word 'all' naturally includes the first, so excluding him does not fit the text.

steps.title: 'All of them' means all the damaged ones
steps.stepSummary: רב אדא בר אהבה explains that 'all of them' refers only to the people who were damaged, which leaves out the first person.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אדא בר אהבה said: 'All of them' means the ones who were damaged.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אדא בר אהבה defends the previous answer by explaining what group the word 'all' refers to.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first person tripped on his own; nobody else knocked him down. Everyone after him was hurt by someone who fell before him. So 'all' means everyone in the group of damaged people, and that group does not include the first.

phrases.english: Rav Adda bar Ahava said:
"All of them" means those who were damaged.

steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'All' means every person in the case.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'All' means all the damaged people, which excludes the first.

steps.title: Then why not just say 'the damaged ones'?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא questions רב אדא בר אהבה: if the ברייתא meant only the damaged ones, it should have said 'הניזקין' and not the confusing word 'כולן'.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is this? If you say it includes even the first, that explains why it says 'all of them.' But if you say it excludes the first, why say 'all of them'? It should have said 'the damaged ones'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רב אדא בר אהבה's reading by asking why the ברייתא used such a misleading word.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'All' fits naturally only if the first is included. If the ברייתא really meant only the damaged people, the clear wording would have been 'הניזקין'. So the word choice seems to support the reading that contradicts רבא.

keyTerms.meaning: What is this? A way of rejecting an answer as not convincing
Let it teach; it should have said

steps.confusionAlert: This is not the end of the discussion. The next step answers this by explaining רבא in a new way, so do not conclude that רבא is refuted.

phrases.english: What is this?
Granted, if you say it includes even the first,
that is why it teaches "all of them";
but if you say it excludes the first,
what is the point of "all of them"?
Let it teach "those who were damaged"!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב אדא בר אהבה's answer in Step 5.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב אדא בר אהבה's reading that 'כולן' means only the damaged ones.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the ברייתא meant only the damaged ones, it would have said 'הניזקין'. Using 'כולן' suggests it includes the first.

steps.title: A new explanation of רבא: the fallen person is like a pit
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא drops the earlier way of reading רבא. Now רבא says the first is liable for the second's body and property. The second is liable for the third's body but not his property, because a person lying on the road counts as a בור, and a בור is never liable for כלים.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רבא said: The first is liable for the second's body damage and property damage. The second is liable for the third's body damage but not property damage. Why? Because the second is like a pit, and a pit is never liable for damaged vessels.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives up on defending the old reading of רבא and explains him in a completely new way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Before, רבא split things into damage done by a person's body versus damage done by his property. Now the split depends on who caused the fall. The first person is fully liable. The second person only lies there like a בור, and the rule is that a בור does not pay for broken כלים. This fits the ברייתא's 'exempt for property damage' without the trouble over the word 'כולן'.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather: we drop what we said before
Pit: one of the main categories of damage
Vessels or objects. A בור is exempt for damaging them.

steps.confusionAlert: Here 'body' and 'property' describe what got damaged on the victim. In the old reading, they described what did the damaging.

phrases.english: Rather, Rava said:
The first is liable
both for damage to the body of the second
and for damage to the property of the second;
and the second is liable for the damages of the third
for damage to his body,
but not for damage to his property.
What is the reason?
Because he is a pit,
phrases.notes: The second person is lying on the road after his fall, so the third trips over him the way someone trips into a pit.

phrases.english: and we have not found a pit
for which one is liable for vessels.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 6 by replacing the whole earlier reading of רבא
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבא split damage done by the body from damage done by property, so the ברייתא's 'כולן' clashed with him
steps.terutzMaskana: רבא splits the first (fully liable) from the second (a בור, exempt for כלים), which fits the ברייתא

steps.title: This works for שמואל but not for רב
steps.stepSummary: Calling the fallen person a בור fits שמואל, who says any obstacle is a בור. רב says an obstacle is only a בור if its owner made it ownerless. A person never makes his own body ownerless, so how can he be a בור?
steps.simpleTranslation: This works for שמואל, who says any obstacle is a pit. But רב says it is a pit only if the owner made it ownerless, and not otherwise. What can we say according to him?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the new explanation from step 7, because it only works according to one opinion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 7 depends on treating the fallen person like a בור. רב holds that an object left in the street counts as a בור only after its owner gives up ownership of it (הפקר). Nobody gives up ownership of his own body, so according to רב the fallen person cannot be a בור.

keyTerms.meaning: This works well (for one opinion, but not for the other)
An obstacle that people trip over
What is there to say? A challenge formula

phrases.english: This works well for Shmuel, who says:
Any obstacle is a pit;
but according to Rav, who says:
if he made it ownerless, yes (it is a pit),
if not, no;
what is there to say?
phrases.notes: The person who fell surely never made his own body ownerless, so according to רב he can't be a pit.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the new explanation of step 7
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim in step 7 that the fallen person counts as a בור
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: According to רב, an obstacle is a בור only if its owner made it ownerless, and a body is never made ownerless

steps.title: Back to the first explanation: vessels damaged by vessels
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא goes back to the original reading of רבא. It answers the ברייתא's 'כולן חייבין' with רב אדא בר מניומי's explanation: the case is one where כלים were damaged by כלים.
steps.simpleTranslation: Really, it is as we said at first. As for your difficulty from 'all of them are liable', רב אדא בר מניומי explained it before רבינא: the case is where vessels were damaged by vessels.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא drops the explanation from step 7, returns to the original reading of רבא, and gives a new answer to the ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The original problem was that 'כולן' seemed to include the first person in the exemption for property damage. The answer is that the ברייתא's exemption is about one person's כלים breaking on another person's כלים. Fallen כלים count as a בור, and a בור is exempt for כלים. So even the first person can be included in 'כולן' without clashing with רבא.

keyTerms.meaning: Actually: we keep the original position

steps.whatToRemember: Final reading: רבא splits body damage from property damage. The ברייתא's exemption is about כלים breaking on כלים, which falls under the rule that a בור is exempt for כלים.

phrases.english: Actually, it is as we said at first,
phrases.notes: Back to the very first reading of רבא, where damage by a person's body and damage by his property are treated differently.

phrases.english: and as for what was difficult for you, "all of them are liable" —

phrases.aramaic: תַּרְגְּמַהּ רַב אַדָּא בַּר מִנְיוֹמֵי קַמֵּיהּ דְּרָבִינָא:
phrases.english: Rav Adda bar Minyumi explained it before Ravina:
where vessels were damaged by vessels.
phrases.notes: The later person's things broke on the earlier person's fallen things, which are like a pit, so there is no payment.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Responds to step 8 by dropping step 7 and answering the original קשיא of step 2 in a new way
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing the case of the ברייתא
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא's exemption for property damage covers the first person in every case, which contradicts רבא
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא is talking about כלים damaged by כלים, where the rules of בור exempt everyone

steps.title: How could everyone fall because of the first person?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the ברייתא's line that if all of them fell because of the first, the first pays for everyone. It then asks how such a case could actually happen.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Master said: If they fell because of the first, the first is liable for all of their damages. How could they fall because of the first?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic. It quotes another line from the ברייתא and asks what that case looks like in real life.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Usually each person trips over the one who fell just before him, so each would be responsible only for the next person. The ברייתא says all of them fell because of the first person, so the גמרא wants to know how one person's fall could trip everyone directly.

phrases.english: The Master said:
If they fell because of the first,
the first is liable for the damages of all of them.
How did they fall because of the first?

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר מָר: אִם מֵחֲמַת רִאשׁוֹן נָפְלוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins a new clarification of another line in the ברייתא
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The physical setup in which all of the people fall directly because of the first person

steps.title: רב פפא: he blocked the whole road
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא explains that the first person fell and stretched across the whole road, like a skeleton, so everyone tripped on him.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: He blocked the road like a skeleton.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא answers the question from step 10 by describing how the first person was lying.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the first person's body covered the full width of the road, nobody could get past him. Each person tripped over a different part of his body, so they all fell because of him and not because of each other.

keyTerms.meaning: Skeleton or carcass, lying stretched out

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said:
Where he blocked the road like a skeleton.
phrases.notes: His body lay across the whole width of the road, so each person tripped over a different part of him.

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The first person's body blocked the entire width of the road

steps.title: רב זביד: he lay slanted like a blind man's cane
steps.stepSummary: רב זביד explains that the first person lay slanted across the road, like a blind man's cane, so everyone tripped on him.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב זביד said: Like a blind man's cane.
steps.whatsHappening: רב זביד gives a different picture of how everyone could have tripped over the first person.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A blind person holds his cane out at an angle. רב זביד means the first person fell diagonally across the road in the same way, so people coming along tripped over him at different points.

phrases.english: Rav Zevid said:
Like a blind man's cane.
phrases.notes: He fell slanted across the road, the way a blind person holds his cane out at an angle.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second answer to the question of step 10, different from רב פפא's
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The first person lay diagonally across the road, like a blind man's cane

steps.title: Barrel and beam coming from opposite directions
steps.stepSummary: The משנה rules that if a barrel breaks against a beam while two people walk toward each other, the beam carrier is פטור, because each one had the right to walk there.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: One person is walking with his barrel and another is walking with his wooden beam. The first one's jug breaks on the other one's beam. The beam carrier is exempt, because each of them had permission to walk in the street.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It describes two people meeting in the street, and the beam breaks the barrel. The משנה says the beam carrier does not have to pay.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The key reason is רשות להלך: both people were allowed to be in רשות הרבים carrying their things. Since the beam carrier did nothing wrong by walking there, he is not blamed for the damage.

keyTerms.meaning: Short for מַתְנִיתִין, 'our משנה'. It marks the start of a new משנה.
A barrel or large clay jug
Permission to walk. Each person has the right to be in the public street.
Exempt; he does not have to pay

steps.confusionAlert: Don't assume that whoever's object did the breaking must pay. Here the beam broke the barrel, and the beam carrier is still פטור, because he was walking where he was allowed to walk.

phrases.english: MISHNAH: This one came with his barrel
and that one came with his beam,
phrases.notes: They are coming toward each other from opposite directions.

phrases.english: this one's jug was broken
by that one's beam: he is exempt;
phrases.notes: The 'jug' here is the same barrel from the first line. 'He' means the beam carrier.

phrases.english: because this one has permission to walk,
and that one has permission to walk.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִי׳ זֶה בָּא בְּחָבִיתוֹ וְזֶה בָּא בְּקוֹרָתוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה after the גמרא finished explaining how everyone could trip over the first person in the road.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When a barrel breaks on a beam as two people walk toward each other in רשות הרבים, the beam carrier is פטור, since both had רשות להלך.

steps.title: Beam carrier in front, barrel carrier behind
steps.stepSummary: The משנה adds a second case. The beam carrier walks first and the barrel carrier follows behind. If the barrel breaks on the beam, the beam carrier is again פטור.
steps.simpleTranslation: If the beam carrier was walking in front and the barrel carrier was walking behind him, and the barrel broke on the beam, the owner of the beam is exempt.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives a second case where both people walk in the same direction, with the beam carrier in front. The beam carrier is still exempt.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the barrel carrier is the one walking behind, so the beam was right in front of him where he could see it. The משנה does not state a new reason, but the ruling stays the same: the person walking ahead with the beam is not responsible.

keyTerms.meaning: The owner of the beam (the beam carrier)

steps.whatToRemember: In both cases in this משנה, opposite directions and beam in front, the beam carrier is פטור when the barrel breaks on his beam.

phrases.english: If the owner of the beam was first
and the owner of the barrel was last;
and the barrel was broken by the beam:
the owner of the beam is exempt.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָיָה בַּעַל הַקּוֹרָה רִאשׁוֹן וּבַעַל חָבִית אַחֲרוֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same משנה with a second arrangement of the two walkers. This time they walk in the same direction instead of toward each other.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When the beam carrier walks in front and the barrel carrier walks behind, and the barrel breaks on the beam, the beam carrier is פטור.
